final_proof:
As usual, a smooth manifold is Hausdorff, and saying that the subset L is diffeomorphic to an open interval means that L carries the subspace topology. Since every open interval is diffeomorphic to ℝ, fix a homeomorphism

f: ℝ → L.

Regarded as a map into X, f is continuous and injective. Call p ∈ X an accumulation point of the positive end of L if there is a sequence t_n → +∞ for which f(t_n) → p, and define accumulation points of the negative end analogously.

We first show that the positive end has at most one accumulation point. Suppose to the contrary that distinct points p,q ∈ X are both accumulation points of that end. Thus there are sequences a_n,b_n → +∞ such that

f(a_n) → p and f(b_n) → q.

Because X is a Hausdorff one-manifold, we can choose a chart φ: O → (−2,2) such that φ(p)=0, q ∉ O, and then set W = φ⁻¹((−1,1)). The set φ⁻¹([−1,1]) is compact and hence closed in X. It follows directly from the chart that

cl(W) = φ⁻¹([−1,1]) and ∂W = {φ⁻¹(−1), φ⁻¹(1)}.

In particular, q ∉ cl(W). Eventually f(a_n) ∈ W, while eventually f(b_n) ∉ cl(W). Since both parameter sequences tend to +∞, we may choose terms from them alternately, obtaining

u₁ < v₁ < u₂ < v₂ < ⋯

such that f(u_i) ∈ W and f(v_i) ∉ cl(W) for every i.

For each i, let

r_i = sup{t ∈ [u_i,v_i] : f(t) ∈ W}.

This set is nonempty because it contains u_i. Since W is open and f(u_i) ∈ W, we have r_i > u_i; since X ∖ cl(W) is open and contains f(v_i), we have r_i < v_i. Points of f⁻¹(W) approach r_i from below, so f(r_i) ∈ cl(W). On the other hand, f(r_i) ∉ W, because otherwise openness of f⁻¹(W) would give points larger than r_i that still belong to the displayed set. Hence f(r_i) ∈ ∂W. The intervals [u_i,v_i] are pairwise disjoint, so the r_i are all distinct. This is impossible: injectivity of f would send these infinitely many distinct parameters to distinct points, whereas ∂W has only two points. Thus the positive end has at most one accumulation point. Applying the same argument to t ↦ f(−t) shows that the negative end also has at most one accumulation point.

It remains to show that every point of cl(L) ∖ L is an accumulation point of one of these two ends. Let p ∈ cl(L) ∖ L. A manifold is first countable, because a chart provides a countable neighborhood base, so there is a sequence x_n ∈ L with x_n → p. Write t_n = f⁻¹(x_n). The sequence (t_n) cannot be bounded. Indeed, if it were bounded, the Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem would give a subsequence t_{n_k} → t ∈ ℝ. Continuity of f would then imply x_{n_k} = f(t_{n_k}) → f(t) ∈ L. But the same subsequence converges to p, and limits in the Hausdorff space X are unique. Hence p = f(t) ∈ L, a contradiction. Therefore (t_n) is unbounded. It consequently has a subsequence tending either to +∞ or to −∞, so p is an accumulation point of the corresponding end.

Every point of cl(L) ∖ L is therefore associated with one of the two ends, and each end has at most one accumulation point. Consequently |cl(L) ∖ L| ≤ 2, which proves the claim.
